key_insight: ASPIS-Net combines acoustic and electrical signals with physics-informed learning to classify CMT weld penetration states and derive explicit equations for interpretation.
engineering_relevance: Noise-resistant, interpretable weld-state monitoring could support quality assurance and structural reliability assessment of welded joints.
method: Dual-branch network processes synchronized acoustic and electrical signals.
Adaptive gated fusion suppresses environmental noise while preserving critical features.
Symbolic regression converts learned representations into explicit equations linked to welding thermodynamics.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 5,000 synchronized samples across four penetration states, reporting 99.36% classification accuracy and 75.59% Macro-F1 under 0 dB composite noise.
watch_item: Generalization to different welding equipment and industrial conditions, and independent validation of the inferred physical equations, remain to be established.
paper_title: Physics-informed multi-sensor fusion framework for predicting weld penetration state and mechanistic discovery in CMT welding
